name: Steps to Take When an Uninsured Driver Causes Your Accident

step.name: Step 1: Prioritize Safety and Seek Medical Attention. First and foremost, check for injuries. If anyone is hurt, call 911 immediately. Even if you feel fine, it's wise to get a medical check-up as soon as possible. Some injuries, like whiplash, don't show up right away. Medical records create a crucial link between the accident and your injuries.

step.name: Step 2: Report the Accident to the Police. Call the local police to report the accident. An official police report is vital for your claim, regardless of the other driver's insurance status. Make sure the report accurately reflects that the other driver was uninsured if that information is available at the scene.

step.name: Step 3: Gather Information and Evidence. Collect as much information as you can from the scene. Get the other driver’s name, contact information, and license plate number. Take photos of both vehicles' damage, the accident scene, and any relevant road conditions. Look for witnesses and get their contact details. Documenting everything thoroughly is key, especially since there won't be an insurance company to easily contact on the other side.

step.name: Step 4: Notify Your Own Insurance Company. Even if the other driver is at fault, you'll need to notify your own insurance provider. Explain that the other driver was uninsured. This is where your Uninsured Motorist (UM) coverage, if you have it, becomes incredibly important. UM coverage is designed to protect you in situations like this. Be careful about giving a recorded statement without first understanding your rights and options.

step.name: Step 5: Consult with an Experienced Uninsured Motorist Accident Lawyer. This is a critical step because uninsured motorist claims can be surprisingly complex, even when dealing with your own insurer. An attorney, like Brett Peterson, can help you understand your policy, negotiate with your insurance company, and ensure you get the full compensation you deserve for medical bills, lost wages, and pain and suffering. They’ll also help you avoid common mistakes that could jeopardize your claim and provide the personalized attention you need.
